title: Building-Agent: A 3D generation agent framework integrating large language models and graph-based 3D generation model
inputData: 自然语言设计任务 + Rhinoceros场地向量与图结构空间数据
contribution: 提出Building-Agent，将GPT-4的任务理解与决策能力和图神经网络的3D生成能力结合，以图结构表示场地和建筑空间，支持自然语言驱动的3D建筑布局生成、自评估与多轮迭代。
abstract: Building-Agent addresses the gap between language understanding and three-dimensional architectural generation by combining an LLM with a graph-based 3D generation model. Real design briefs and site constraints are used to test task processing. The framework reasons over graph representations of 3D site information and natural-language requirements, predicts building layouts, and supports interactive multi-step natural-language iteration.
methodology: Vector site data from Rhinoceros are encoded as graph-structured 3D data whose nodes contain geometric and positional attributes and whose edges encode spatial adjacency. GPT-4 receives the design-task text and serialized graph information, then outputs graph-structured 3D vectors representing building-layout decisions. A pretrained Building-GNN consumes these graph outputs to generate voxelized 3D layouts. Generated layouts are checked against evaluation indicators extracted from the design brief; unsatisfied designs trigger self-iteration, while acceptable designs are output as 3D models.
results: Experiments with real design briefs and site constraints show that Building-Agent can predict site-layout outcomes with high task-completion performance and can iteratively adjust 3D building layouts through multi-step natural-language instructions. The study demonstrates that explicit graph representations can bridge LLM reasoning and downstream 3D generation.
taskEn: 3D building layout generation and iterative refinement
inputDataEn: Natural-language design tasks plus Rhinoceros site vectors and graph-structured spatial data
operationEvidence: GPT-4 generates graph-structured layout decisions; the generated graph is executed by the pretrained Building-GNN to create a 3D layout, and the workflow evaluates the generated form against design-task indicators to decide whether self-iteration is required.
